chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding five young camels (qala'is) is one sheep, and there is nothing regarding less than five; and regarding ten are two sheep, and regarding fifteen are three sheep, and regarding twenty are four (sheep), and regarding twenty-five are five (sheep), and regarding twenty-six is a Bint Makhad (a young female camel in its fourth year) up to thirty-five.

And Abd al-Rahman said, 'This is a difference between us and the people. So when it is increased by one, so regarding these would be a Bint Labun (a young female camel in its fifth year) up to forty-five. So when it is increased by one, so regarding these would be a Hiqqah (a mature female camel in its sixth year) up to sixty. So when it increases by one, so regarding these would be a Jadh'ah (a young female camel in its seventh year) up to seventy-five. So when it increases by one, so regarding these would be two Bint Labun up to ninety. So when there are more camels, so regarding every fifty would be a Hiqqah.'

key_terms.بِنْتُ لَبُونٍ: A young female camel in her fifth year, named so because she yields abundant milk
key_terms.بِنْتُ مَخَاضٍ: A young female camel in her fourth year, named so because she is about to give birth
key_terms.جَذَعَةٌ: A young female camel in her seventh year
key_terms.حِقَّةٌ: A mature female camel in her sixth year
key_terms.خَمْسٌ: The number five, used here as a base unit for counting sheep or camels in Zakat calculations
key_terms.قَلَائِصَ: Young camels (specifically those in their third to fifth year)

ai.seo_question: What is the Zakat ruling for a herd of camels according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi outlines the precise nisab and distribution of Zakat for camels, highlighting the distinct Shia methodology that differentiates it from Sunni schools through specific age-based classifications like Bint Makhad and Hiqqah. It emphasizes the incremental increase in liability as the herd grows, reflecting the jurisprudential emphasis on fairness and gradual obligation in Shia fiqh.
